newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RESEARCH INSTITUTE SEES 2PCT GDP IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RESEARCH INSTITUTE SEES 2PCT GDP IN 1997.

text.p: Hungarian think-tank Kopint-Datorg Rt said on Wednesday it expected a small economic growth on the back of a mild rise of consumption and a more spectacular growth in investments.
"Our prognosis for 1997 says there's potential for a relatively moderate, two percent GDP growth," Kopint-Datorg deputy chief executive Andras Koves told a news conference.
"This (growth) would materialise amid a minimal growth in consumption and a stronger, eight to 10 percent growth in investments."
The government's GDP growth target is similarly two percent, but it is hopeful of a 10 to 12 percent investment growth.

The Central Statistical Office (KSH) recently released a GDP growth figure of one percent for 1996, while Kopint-Datorg and other think-tanks had previously forecast flat economic performance for 1996.
Koves said a quicker rise in inflation than in nominal wages was a risk factor as it would undermine economic growth by reducing household consumption.
"First among risks we mention the consumption," he said. "It isn't sure that the current level of consumption will remain unchanged."

Kopint-Datorg expects a very mild, virtually unchanged 0.5 percent growth in household consumption this year, Koves said, adding that a decline in consumption could reduce the pace of GDP growth or even hamper it.
Real wages in Hungary fell by five percent last year.
Kopint-Datorg foresees an 18 to 19 percent consumer price inflation for this year, compared to an average of 23.6 percent for last year and a government target of around 18 percent.
The general government budget deficit is seen reaching 4.5 to five percent of the GDP, cvompared with the government's target of 4.9 percent.
